cases.description: When the Position is created with a ZeroCostModel, any call to getHoldingCost(int) should return NaN regardless of the supplied finalIndex.
ZeroCostModel must also return NaN for negative finalIndex values; the method does not perform its own validation.
CustomCostModel returns Num.valueOf(0) when finalIndex == 0. This tests the branch where the index is exactly zero.
CustomCostModel returns Num.valueOf(finalIndex) for positive indices. This covers the 'positive index' branch.
CustomCostModel returns Num.valueOf(finalIndex) for negative indices as well, exercising the 'negative index' branch.

group: CustomCostModel that throws on invalid index

cases.description: The custom CostModel is designed to throw IllegalArgumentException when finalIndex < 0. The Position#getHoldingCost method should propagate this exception.

If a Position is instantiated with a null holdingCostModel (e.g., via reflection or a faulty constructor), calling getHoldingCost should raise a NullPointerException because the method dereferences the field.
A CostModel implementation that deliberately returns null from calculate(...). The Position#getHoldingCost method should forward this null value without throwing an exception.

group: CustomCostModel returning NaN for a specific index

cases.description: CostModel returns Num.NaN only when finalIndex equals 42. This verifies that Position#getHoldingCost propagates NaN exactly as produced by the model.
For any index other than 42 the same CostModel returns Num.valueOf(finalIndex). Ensures normal values are still passed through.
A mock CostModel records the Position instance received in calculate(...). The test asserts that the recorded reference is the same Position object on which getHoldingCost was invoked.
Using Integer.MAX_VALUE to ensure the method correctly forwards very large positive indices to the CostModel.
Using Integer.MIN_VALUE to verify that extreme negative indices are handled (no overflow) and passed unchanged to the CostModel.

group: CostModel that depends on Position state

cases.description: A CostModel calculates holding cost as entryPrice * finalIndex. The Position is created with an entry Trade whose price is Num.valueOf(100). For finalIndex 2 the expected cost is 100 * 2 = 200. This tests that Position#getHoldingCost forwards the Position itself so the model can inspect its trades.
Same state‑dependent CostModel, but with finalIndex 0, should yield a cost of 0, confirming correct handling of zero multiplier.
A custom CostModel implementation is programmed to throw IllegalStateException for any index. Position#getHoldingCost should propagate this unchecked exception unchanged.
A custom CostModel throws ArithmeticException when finalIndex is negative. The method must not catch it and should let the exception bubble up.
The CostModel's calculate method deliberately throws a NullPointerException (e.g., due to a bug). Position#getHoldingCost should forward this exception rather than masking it.
A CostModel implementation throws an AssertionError (or any subclass of java.lang.Error). Position#getHoldingCost must not catch Errors; they should propagate to the caller.
